title: Joining Mezz Mezzrow's 1954 European tour
summary: Moore replaced Zutty with Mezzrow, playing washboard, drums and vocals at the Olympia in Paris.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I see. Well, after leaving de Paris, then you found yourself with Mezz Mezzrow. You went with Mezz?
'54, yeah. And you had a chance to go to Europe with Mezz.
How did that date come up, going to Europe with Mezz Mezzrow and...?
That's when we played at the Olympia Theatre.

You played the Olympia. Did you play the Salle Pleyel in Paris? Because there are some recordings with Mezz Mezzrow in November of '54... But what did he do? He contacted you and he said he was going abroad?

No, I worked with him a little bit here in New York. He used to sit in... He had the band down at Jimmy Ryan's for a little while, after... I was down there with Sidney Bechet for a while. Then Sidney Bechet got a chance

to go to Europe, and he put Mezzrow in his place for a while. I don't know what happened. But anyway, I was with Mezzrow for a while. Something happened down at Jimmy Ryan's, and that's when they decided to get ...(? )...(? )... somebody's name(?) anyway...

But Mezz went to Europe, and stayed over there a long time. He had been there before, I think. He learned to speak the language. And during that time, that's when he wrote that book, Really The Blues -- I think it was that time. But he decided he wanted to... He got a lot of dates lined up, and he had... I think he had Zuddy over there doing something; he had Zuddy before me. Then they got over to me, and I was over there after Zuddy. They had a big run-in or something, he and Zuddy, they had a fight or something. So I got a call and I came out there.
For the recording(?) date... He played two or three more days to kind of warm up before going into the Olympia Theatre, because that's a big place...
